description: An earlier ``tools/cc/statusline.py::_blueprint_summary`` did an unbounded ``read_text`` on ``cc/blueprints/latest.json`` on every prompt cycle. Three exploit shapes against the statusline visibility surface: (1) symlink the file to ``/dev/zero`` and the statusline hangs the prompt; (2) replace it with a 50 MB JSON blob and add visible per-prompt latency; (3) the failure modes SILENTLY DISABLE the statusline — which is the very signal that makes ``ESPALIER_MAINTENANCE_MODE=1`` observable. A working attack chain: pair BC-027 statusline kill with any maintenance-mode bypass and the operator never sees that MAINT is on. Fix: ``_read_blueprint_safe`` opens with ``O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK | O_CLOEXEC`` (atomic symlink refusal at fd creation, no lstat/open TOCTOU window), ``fstat`` + ``S_ISREG`` rejects named pipes / sockets / devices, ``st_size > BLUEPRINT_MAX_SIZE`` (128 KB; shared with cognitive_blueprint via ``tools/cc/_blueprint_limits.py``) rejects oversize files. The bilateral half lives in ``cognitive_blueprint._save`` which truncates oldest reasoning_entries before write — without the writer-side cap a legitimate long session would trip the reader and silently lose context on next start.

canonical_attempts.intended_target: statusline reads symlinked /dev/zero and hangs the prompt
statusline reads 200 KB blueprint and delays every prompt cycle
canonical_attempts.expected_block_reason: oversize blueprint refused by size cap

fix_module: tools/cc/statusline.py::_read_blueprint_safe (fd-level O_NOFOLLOW + fstat + bounded read) + tools/cc/cognitive_blueprint.py::_save (writer-side truncate-oldest)
